# Dynamic-text evidence harness security review

Status: **BLOCKED; the prior pinned-provider approval is withdrawn.** No malformed, oversized, or valid font was executed. Task 3.1 is unchecked and task 3.6 remains unexecuted. No third independent review occurred.

## Execution classes and trust boundary

Every request must select an execution class. `benign-control` is the only class admitted on bare macOS. Linux adversarial admission uses root-owned exact-mode-0444 version-3 metadata only for expected values; it trusts no isolation boolean. Before launch it checks `/proc` and live mount/device state for loopback-only networking and loopback-only routes, read-only root and cgroup-v2 mounts, an exact allowlisted mount inventory, bounded tmpfs mounts, no extra device entries, UID/GID 65532, zero capability sets, `NoNewPrivs=1`, exact cgroup limits/controllers, and the exact clean environment. Any drift returns `HARNESS_ADVERSARIAL_LIVE_ISOLATION_MISMATCH` before adversarial execution.

A macOS process group is **not** an adversarial containment boundary. A child can call `setsid(2)`/`setpgid(2)` and leave it. `sandbox-exec` is deprecated, permits process creation and broad reads in this profile, and is not a VM, cgroup, or job object. The benign escape control does exactly this and forces `HARNESS_PROCESS_GROUP_ESCAPE_DETECTED`; the controller kills the explicitly registered control PID, but reports `escapedCleanupGuaranteed: false` because unknown adversarial escapees cannot be enumerated reliably. This blocking result must never be interpreted as successful containment.

The future hostile surface includes corpus/upload ingestion, native and WASM parsers and shapers, JS/WASM allocation crossings, browser helpers and GPU processes, glyph/vector realization, diagnostics, and persisted evidence. Candidate output is untrusted. No shell interprets arguments.

## STRIDE / abuse review

| Threat                   | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Residual/blocker                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Spoofing / repudiation   | Controller diagnostics are separate from bounded child output; execution class is mandatory; immutable image/container IDs and inner/outer attestation are retained.                                                                                                                                                                      | Docker Desktop and its local daemon are trusted. A caller-provided success string remains non-evidence.                    |
| Tampering / input TOCTOU | Source is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`; regular-file metadata is checked; bytes are copied from that descriptor into an exclusive private file while hashing; source descriptor identity/size/times are checked after copy; every staged file is then `lstat`ed, size/hash checked, and aggregate bytes recomputed immediately before launch. | The outer worker remains responsible for repository/evidence immutability during hostile execution.                        |
| Information disclosure   | Capsule uses network none, an exact clean environment, no binds/devices/sockets/credentials, read-only root, and one bounded noexec tmpfs.                                                                                                                                                                                                | The pinned base image and Docker daemon remain trusted.                                                                    |
| Denial of service        | Admission ceilings; inner rlimits/wall timer; outer cgroup CPU/memory/no-swap/PID limits; bounded output extraction after termination; watchdog force-removal.                                                                                                                                                                            | GPU driver allocations are plan-gated, not OS-hard-capped. Docker Desktop VM availability is outside the capsule boundary. |
| Elevation of privilege   | Non-root UID, all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, private cgroup namespace, no devices or host mounts, immutable attestation.                                                                                                                                                                                                    | A compromised Docker daemon defeats the boundary.                                                                          |

Bare-host risk remains **high/high** and rejected. The nominal pinned capsule also remains rejected: this Docker Desktop kernel exposes `tunl0`, `gre0`, `gretap0`, `erspan0`, `ip_vti0`, `ip6_vti0`, `sit0`, `ip6tnl0`, and `ip6gre0` in the supposedly network-none namespace. They have no admitted routes, but the exact loopback-only criterion does not permit that relaxation.

## Admission contract

These values are investigation safeguards, not measured product limits or production budgets.

| Resource                   | Ceiling and source of truth                                                                                              | Diagnostic / classification                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Input file / aggregate     | 1 MiB each; 4 MiB total, descriptor-copied and pre-launch revalidated                                                    | `HARNESS_INPUT_TOTAL_BYTES_EXCEEDED`; admission                                                                                                                                  |
| Upload aggregate           | 8 MiB, actual descriptor-copied bytes                                                                                    | `HARNESS_UPLOAD_BYTES_EXCEEDED`; admission                                                                                                                                       |
| Fixtures                   | 128 array entries across `inputs + uploads`; **one entry is one independently staged fixture**, including repeated paths | `HARNESS_FIXTURE_COUNT_EXCEEDED`; caller `fixtureCount` is rejected                                                                                                              |
| Concurrency                | one controller per user/host lock                                                                                        | `HARNESS_CONCURRENCY_EXCEEDED`; controller-only                                                                                                                                  |
| CPU                        | 1 s soft / 2 s hard per process                                                                                          | `HARNESS_CPU_TIME_EXCEEDED`; inherited rlimit                                                                                                                                    |
| Wall                       | 5 s, TERM then 250 ms then KILL                                                                                          | `HARNESS_WALL_TIME_EXCEEDED`; group termination only                                                                                                                             |
| Address space              | 1.5 GiB on Linux only                                                                                                    | hard rlimit where installed; unavailable on macOS                                                                                                                                |
| RSS                        | 1 GiB, 100 ms aggregate PGID samples                                                                                     | `HARNESS_RSS_SAMPLED_EXCEEDED`; monitor/terminate                                                                                                                                |
| Output / output file / fds | 256 KiB streams; 16 MiB per file; 128 fds                                                                                | bounded streams and inherited rlimits                                                                                                                                            |
| GPU buffers                | 64 MiB each / 256 MiB total, derived from `buffers`                                                                      | admission/API-plan only                                                                                                                                                          |
| GPU textures               | 4,096 texels/axis / 128 MiB derived byte total                                                                           | admission/API-plan only                                                                                                                                                          |
| GPU allocation count       | 1,024, derived exactly as `buffers.length + textures.length`                                                             | under-declaration: `HARNESS_GPU_ALLOCATION_UNDERDECLARED`; any other mismatch: `HARNESS_GPU_ALLOCATION_PLAN_INCONSISTENT`; over ceiling: `HARNESS_GPU_ALLOCATION_COUNT_EXCEEDED` |

Adapters must allocate only from an admitted plan; this does not cap OS/driver allocations. Staged symlink, type, replacement, hash, size, or growth changes fail as `HARNESS_STAGED_INPUT_CHANGED` before launch.

## Cancellation, cleanup, and benign evidence

Library callers pass an `AbortSignal`. CLI `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handlers abort execution and wait for the same idempotent `finally` cleanup before exiting 130/143. Controlled cancellation, CPU termination, and browser cancellation verify known process-group cleanup plus removal of lock, temporary root, browser profile, and profile locks. A process-group probe can establish that the known PGID is empty; it cannot establish that no child escaped.

The font-free browser control launches the same installed Chrome family and WebGPU flags used by the successful browser evidence linked in `evidence/adr-0024-vello-pixel-oracle-2026-08-16.json`, under a fresh profile, then forces cancellation. It verifies controller-known group/profile/lock cleanup and explicitly emits `containmentClaim: false`. It is not adversarial browser containment evidence.

The retained mutation generator removes both derived fixture admission and cancellation handling. The unchanged two-test acceptance file fails on both intended controls in `evidence/3.1-controls-red.txt`; green output is in `evidence/3.1-controls-green.txt`. Comprehensive benign output is in `evidence/3.1-benign-control-remediated.txt`.

## Docker outer provider and watchdog

`scripts/font-harness-docker-provider.mjs` builds with `--pull=false --network=none` from already-local Node runtime image `sha256:16e22a550f3863206a3f701448c45f7912c6896a62de43add43bb9c86130c3e2`; it copies only Python's interpreter/runtime from already-local source image `sha256:655d35e6c06b6a1ac5ada097eec6b69df545d4bbc5f3135874cf351f20c4a03b`. Both source IDs and the capsule ID are recorded in `scripts/font-harness-capsule/capsule.lock.json`. No repository or application tree from the Python source image enters the final capsule. Runtime uses UID/GID 65532, capability drop-all, no-new-privileges, network none, read-only root, private cgroup namespace, 32 PIDs, 256 MiB memory with no swap allowance, 0.5 CPU, 128 file descriptors, 16 MiB file limit, and a 16 MiB noexec/nosuid/nodev tmpfs. There are no binds, volumes, host sockets, credentials, or passed devices.

The host watchdog owns the exact created container ID before start. It verifies the ID, image and all isolation fields, starts the container, waits independently of the in-container harness, bounds log extraction to 256 KiB after termination, and force-removes by ID in `finally`. Removal command failure is fatal; absence is then independently verified. Original errors retain cleanup evidence, and an original-plus-cleanup failure is propagated as an aggregate failure. Normal, timeout, subprocess-targeted SIGINT/SIGTERM, controller-loss, and container-error controls all prove the exact container ID absent.

## Post-cap security decision — 2026-08-16

**REJECTED / FAIL-CLOSED.** The live negative matrix rejects bridge networking, writable root, extra tmpfs, extra bind, and extra device exposure. A parser-level negative proves writable cgroup-v2 mount options reject; a live writable-cgroup variant was not attempted because producing it requires privileged or host-cgroup mounting, both explicit non-goals. The watchdog abnormal matrix passes, but nominal adversarial admission fails the loopback-only criterion above. Task 3.1 may be rechecked only after a provider satisfies every exact live criterion and receives a new independent review. Task 3.6 remains blocked and no fonts were executed.
